match_phrases: there are no shipping rates available
explanation: Checkout found zero rates for that address. Almost always a missing country in a shipping zone, a weight/price condition the cart does not meet, or a carrier account that returned nothing.
steps: Reproduce it: create an order or use a draft order with the customer's city, country, and postal code.
Go to Settings → Shipping and delivery → Shipping → Manage rates.
Open every profile and confirm the customer's country sits in exactly one zone with at least one rate.
Add a fallback flat rate (for example "Standard · any weight") so a carrier API failure cannot zero out checkout.
If you use carrier-calculated rates, open the carrier account and confirm the API credentials are still valid.

match_phrases: this country is already in a zone
explanation: A country or region can only live in one zone per shipping profile. Overlaps make Shopify pick an unexpected rate or show none.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery → Manage rates.
Expand each zone and write down which countries it contains.
If the United States (or another country) appears twice, remove it from the wrong zone.
Use Rest of world only as a true catch-all — not in addition to every country listed elsewhere.
Save and retest checkout with that country's address.

explanation: Products in a custom shipping profile do not use the General profile rates. If that custom profile has no zone for the customer, checkout shows no rates — even when General is fully set up.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery → Shipping profiles.
Open each custom profile and check its product list and zones.
Add the missing country/rate to the custom profile, or move the product back to the General profile.
Remember: items from two profiles create a split shipment and the customer pays both rates.
Test with a cart that contains only the problem product, then a mixed cart.

explanation: Live carrier rates fail silently. Expired credentials, an unpaid carrier account, or a package with no weight returns "no shipping methods" instead of a useful error.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery → Couriers (or Carrier accounts).
Reconnect the carrier. Paste new API keys from the carrier dashboard.
Every product in the cart needs a weight. Open Products and fill in weight + package dimensions.
Settings → Shipping and delivery → Packages: define a default package size the carrier will accept.
Keep a flat-rate backup in the same zone so checkout never goes empty if the carrier API times out.

explanation: Weight-based rates skip a cart when items have zero weight, or when the total weight falls between brackets you never created.
steps: Open the product → Shipping and confirm Weight is greater than 0 and This is a physical product is checked.
Settings → Shipping and delivery → the zone's rates. Look at each weight range (for example 0–1 kg, 1–5 kg).
Add a rate that covers 0 weight and a catch-all "and up" bracket.
If you sell digital goods, uncheck This is a physical product so they do not require shipping.
Retest with the exact product that failed.

explanation: Local delivery only appears when the customer's postal code is inside the location's delivery zone and the cart meets the min/max order rules.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery → Local delivery.
Enable local delivery on the correct location (the one that actually holds the inventory).
Add postal codes or a delivery radius that includes the customer. Watch for ZIP+4 vs 5-digit mismatches.
Check the minimum order amount — a $40 minimum will hide delivery on a $25 cart.
The customer must choose a shipping address in that area; a billing-only address will not unlock delivery.
target_ui_hint: Settings > Shipping and delivery > Local delivery

synonyms: customers can't pick up in store
explanation: Pickup only shows when it is enabled on a location that stocks the item and is set as a fulfillment location for that product.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery → Local pickup → enable it on the store location.
Settings → Locations: the location must be active and used to fulfill online orders.
The product must have available inventory at that pickup location (not only at a warehouse across the country).
Write pickup instructions (door, hours). Customers see them after checkout.
Test with a customer address near the store — some themes hide pickup when expected.
target_ui_hint: Settings > Shipping and delivery > Local pickup

synonyms: customers charged when it should be free
explanation: Free shipping can come from a rate, a discount code, or an automatic discount. Conditions (min subtotal, specific products, logged-in customers) often block it.
steps: Decide which mechanism you meant to use: a $0 rate in a zone, or a discount in Shopify admin → Discounts.
If it is a rate: open the zone and check the min price / weight. A "free over $50" rate will not appear on a $49 cart — add a paid rate below that.
If it is a discount: confirm it is Active, not expired, and applies to the customer's products and country.
App discounts and Shopify discounts can conflict. Disable extras and retest.
Preview checkout at $49 and $51 to see both sides of the threshold.
target_ui_hint: Settings > Shipping and delivery > Free rate

explanation: Shopify assigned the order to a location that does not ship to the customer's zone, or the product's inventory is at a location with no matching rates.
steps: Settings → Locations and open each location. Note which ones fulfill online orders.
Settings → Shipping and delivery: each profile can use different location groups. Confirm the stocking location is in the group that has rates for the customer.
Products → the product → Inventory: stock should exist at a location that can ship there.
If you use apps to split locations, disable them briefly to see if rates return.
Place a test order and check which location Shopify assigned under the order's fulfillment card.

explanation: Buying a Shopify Shipping label fails when the address is unverified, the package is missing dimensions, or the store's shipping billing method is invalid.
steps: Open the order → Fulfill item → check the destination address. Fix any failed address verification.
Enter package weight and dimensions. Use a saved package under Settings → Shipping and delivery → Packages.
Settings → Shipping and delivery → Shipping labels: confirm a valid card is on file for postage (this is separate from Shopify Payments payouts).
If a carrier service is down, pick another service level (for example USPS Ground Advantage instead of Priority).
International labels also need HS codes and a customs form on the product.

explanation: International checkout fails when the country is not in a zone, duties are misconfigured, or products lack customs data.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery: add the country to a zone with a real rate (or a Rest of world rate).
Settings → Taxes and duties: decide whether you collect duties at checkout (DDP) or let the carrier collect on delivery (DDU).
Each product needs a country of origin and an HS code under Product → Shipping.
Markets: the international market must be published and include that country.
Test with a non-domestic address and a product that has customs fields filled.

explanation: Checkout UI extensions and shipping apps can hide or replace Shopify rates. A buggy app often presents as "no methods available."
steps: Settings → Apps and sales channels. Disable shipping, delivery, or checkout apps one at a time.
After each disable, retest checkout with the same address.
Settings → Checkout → Customize: look for delivery customizations and turn them off to isolate the issue.
Once you find the app, update it or contact its developer — do not leave checkout broken while you wait.
Keep native Shopify rates as a fallback even when an app is the primary calculator.

synonyms: subscribe and save has no shipping
explanation: Selling plans use the same zones as one-time orders unless a subscription app injects its own rates. Missing customer addresses on recurring orders also blank out rates.
steps: Confirm a normal one-time checkout still shows rates. If not, fix zones first.
Open the subscription app and check its shipping settings — some require their own rate table.
On the customer profile, confirm the shipping address is still valid (expired apartments are common).
Make sure subscription products are in a profile that covers that country.
For a failed recurring order, update the address and retry billing from the subscription contract.

synonyms: ups won't deliver to po box
explanation: UPS and FedEx generally will not deliver to PO Boxes or APO/FPO addresses. If those are your only rates, checkout shows nothing.
steps: Add a USPS (or national postal) rate in the same zone as a fallback — postal services accept PO Boxes.
In the shipping app or carrier settings, allow USPS for residential / PO Box addresses.
Optionally add checkout helper text: "Use a street address for courier delivery."
APO/FPO should be treated as US addresses with USPS, not international.
Retest with a PO Box address and a street address.
target_ui_hint: Settings > Shipping and delivery > Carrier restrictions

explanation: A missing translation does not hide the rate, but a delivery customization that expects a translated handle can drop it.
steps: Settings → Languages (or Markets → languages) and translate each shipping rate name.
Keep the same meaning — checkout apps often match on the English handle.
If a rate vanished only in one language, disable delivery customizations and retest.
Save, then preview checkout in that language from the Markets preview.
Avoid renaming rates in a live store without updating the translations at the same time.

explanation: Draft orders do not auto-apply store rates unless you click Add shipping. Marking an order as Shipping not required will skip rates entirely.
steps: Open the draft order and confirm the shipping address is filled.
Click Add shipping and choose a calculated rate, or enter a custom amount.
If the product is physical, do not check Shipping not required.
Taxes on shipping are controlled under Settings → Taxes and duties.
Send the invoice only after the shipping line is present so the customer is not undercharged.

explanation: The estimate comes from the rate's transit time plus the location's cutoff and processing time. An empty transit time hides the promise or shows a wild range.
steps: Settings → Shipping and delivery → the rate → add a transit time (for example 3–5 business days).
Set order processing time on the location (same page, at the top of the profile).
Enable delivery dates at checkout if you want a calendar instead of a range.
Carrier-calculated rates bring their own ETAs — do not also hardcode a conflicting range.
Remember weekends and the cutoff hour (orders after 2pm often start the next business day).
target_ui_hint: Settings > Shipping and delivery > Transit time

explanation: The product checkbox This is a physical product controls whether checkout asks for a shipping address. The wrong value either blocks digital customers or lets physical orders skip postage.
steps: Open the product → Shipping section.
Physical goods: check This is a physical product and enter a weight.
Digital goods, services, and gift cards: uncheck it.
For mixed bundles, use a bundle app or separate line items so each item follows the right rule.
Save and run checkout — digital-only carts should jump from information to payment.
